sources.title: When a felling licence is needed
sources.role: Official 2026 guidance on felling-licence requirements and exemptions in England.
sources.facts: A licence is generally required to fell growing trees unless an exemption applies; unauthorised felling can be an offence.
sources.guard: General rules do not prove an exemption, licence, tree identity, ownership, safety necessity, planning coverage or lawful felling on a parcel.

sources.title: Apply for a felling licence
sources.role: Official application process for tree-felling licences.
sources.facts: Applicants provide proposed felling and restocking information; approval produces a licence subject to terms and periods.
sources.guard: An application or testing service does not prove licence grant, correct boundaries, compliance, restocking completion or development consent.

sources.title: Understanding tree felling in England
sources.role: Official overview of felling, permissions, constraints and public registers.
sources.facts: Felling proposals should assess environmental, wildlife, historic-environment and landscape constraints and follow the UK Forestry Standard.
sources.guard: An overview or register entry does not prove full constraint assessment, consultation outcome, legality, implementation or sustainable management.

sources.title: Tree felling in England
sources.role: Official collection for licences, management, constraints, changes and illegal felling.
sources.facts: The collection separates permission, sustainable management, circumstances, variations, conditions and enforcement routes.
sources.guard: A collection page does not establish which route applies, whether an offence occurred or whether a proposal is permitted.

sources.title: Tree Preservation Orders and trees in conservation areas
sources.origin: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.role: Official planning guidance on TPOs and conservation-area tree controls.
sources.facts: TPOs protect specified trees, groups or woodland; consent is generally required for prohibited works, with separate conservation-area notification rules.
sources.guard: National guidance does not prove a TPO exists, its map covers a tree, an exception applies, consent was issued or required notices were valid.

sources.title: Ancient woodland, ancient trees and veteran trees: advice for planning decisions
sources.role: Official standing advice for planning proposals affecting irreplaceable habitats.
sources.facts: Ancient woodland and ancient or veteran trees are irreplaceable habitats and are material considerations for LPAs.
sources.guard: Standing advice and inventories do not prove exact habitat boundaries, tree status, impact significance, mitigation adequacy or permission.

sources.title: Planning applications affecting trees and woodland
sources.role: Official guidance on tree and woodland issues in development proposals.
sources.facts: Felling on development sites may still require a Forestry Commission licence unless an exemption or sufficiently explicit planning permission applies.
sources.guard: Planning permission wording must be checked; this guidance does not prove trees are within an approved footprint or exempt from licensing.

sources.title: Definitions of felling and restocking options
sources.role: Official regulatory terminology for licence applications and restocking proposals.
sources.facts: Applications must accurately specify felling type and, where applicable, restocking method using Forestry Commission terminology.
sources.guard: Terminology guidance does not prove an application is accurate, approved, implemented, monitored or compliant with licence conditions.

package_guard: Felling guidance, licence applications, TPO rules, woodland inventories and standing advice do not by themselves prove exact tree or woodland boundaries, protected status, lawful works, consent, exemption, restocking, ecological acceptability, planning permission, funding or delivery.
